exits.failMessage: The Greenway checkpoint is on high alert — the Bulwark has locked down passage until the Nightside threat is resolved. Clear the Spire of Vigil first.

lines: The Civic Center is tense. Hushed arguments in the corridors. Councillor Asha Denn's door is closed — voices behind it, urgent and low.
Thorne is at his usual post, but his posture has changed. He is watching the exits.
Whatever the Array learned from your visit to the Deep Processing facility, the information is already rippling outward. The Council knows something has shifted.

actions.text: Hollis stamps the deed with a heavy seal. 'Lot 7, East Terrace — the old relay station salvage yard. It's yours. Clear it out, build it up.'

actions.prompt: Thorne offers you a data-sharing arrangement with the Array. Better trade rates in exchange for your exploration data.

options.label: Accept
options.description: Share exploration data with the Array for premium trade rates

options.label: Decline
options.description: Keep your data private. Standard trade rates apply.

lines: You agree to share your exploration data with MERIDIAN-7.
Thorne smiles — a practiced, professional smile. 'Wise choice. Your Premium Terminal access is now active at the Array Hub.'

actions.text: You decline the offer. Thorne's smile doesn't waver. 'Of course. The offer remains open, should you reconsider.'
You have the Salvage Yard Deed for Lot 7. The East Terrace is accessible through the gate in the northeast wall. Time to start building your solar infrastructure.

Councillor Denn nods thoughtfully. 'When you're ready to return to the dark perimeter, collect biological samples for me. Fungal cultures, organism tissue, soil from the relay stations. This research could change everything.'

lines: Councillor Asha Denn listens carefully as you describe the Spire of Vigil — the ancient architecture, the pre-human technology, the energy signatures connecting it to the Lighthouse network.
'This confirms what I feared. The Lighthouses aren't independent systems. They're nodes in something much older. And now the Compact knows it too.'
'General Thorne has already briefed the Council. The Compact is invoking emergency security powers — they want military control over every structure that matches the Spire's architecture.'
'The Monument of Winds. That old landmark east of the Greenway. It matches the Spire's profile. The Bulwark is moving to seize it as we speak.'
'I need someone in the Greenway. Someone who can see what the Bulwark is doing and isn't afraid to push back. The checkpoint east of here will let you through — I've arranged clearance.'
Councillor Asha Denn takes one look at your face and closes the door to her office.

You lay out everything: the Deep Processing facility, the central containment vats, the culture medium labeled 7-SIGMA-4. Synthetic amino acids. Chloroplast-analog enzymes. Four million synthesis iterations.
Project Autotroph. The Array's quiet, patient effort to make the Ring's biological leverage obsolete.
Asha listens without interrupting. When you finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her hands are still. Her jaw is tight.
The Council will never look at the Array the same way again.
Thorne sees you coming. His practiced smile flickers once — then steadies, out of habit. But his eyes are different.
He already knows you've been inside the Array complex. MERIDIAN-7 told him. That's his job: to know.

actions.prompt: Councillor Asha Denn notices the data tablet in your hands. Her eyes sharpen.

options.label: Share the symbiosis research
options.description: Give Asha the Array's own proof that cooperation outperforms extraction.

lines: Asha reads the cross-system compatibility data. Halfway through, she sits down.
'The Array's own research. Their own scientists proved it — symbiosis produces superior results. Extraction degrades the compounds. Living ecosystems outperform harvested ones by a factor of twelve.'
'And they buried it. They buried their own evidence because it contradicted a directive they had already committed to.'
'This is the argument I've been looking for. Not ideology — data. The Array's data.'
She produces a sol component from her desk — living circuitry grown from Ring biotech.
'A prototype. Proof of concept that biology and technology can work in concert. It heals as it fights. The beginning of symbiosis, in your hands.'

actions.text: Asha nods. 'The evidence will keep. But the political window will not. Bring it to me when you are ready.'

lines: The alliance is forged. Ring, Unbounded, and Array — three factions, one expedition.
Councillor Asha Denn has authorized the joint Nightside expedition. Sable will guide. The Array will observe. And you will lead.
Meet Sable at the Nightside Passage, beyond the Nightside Depths. The path to the three endings begins here.
Asha takes the compound with trembling hands. She holds it up to the light, watching the crystalline-organic matrix shift and pulse.
'This is it. The proof we needed. A compound that exists only through symbiosis — a living relationship that no synthesis lab can replicate.'
'The Array's Autotroph project will never reproduce this. Biology isn't just chemistry. It's communion.'
'The Council will hear this. All of them. And then... then we decide what comes next. For all three factions.'
'Three paths lie ahead, Lightkeeper. The choice will be yours.'

actions.prompt: The evidence is before the Council. Three paths forward. The choice shapes the future of all three factions — and the planet itself.

options.label: Shut Down the Array
options.description: Side with the Unbounded. Restore the Underlumen. Accept a harder world, but a free one.

options.label: Broker Symbiosis
options.description: Merge Array, Underlumen, and Ring biology into a genuine partnership. The hardest path, but the most hopeful.

options.label: Seize Control
options.description: Take the Array's infrastructure for humanity. Suppress both the Underlumen and Array autonomy. Power at a cost.

actions.prompt: The evidence is before the Council. Two paths forward — a third path exists, known only to those who have walked the deep Nightside and listened. The choice shapes the future of all three factions — and the planet itself.

options.label: Shut Down the Array
options.description: Side with the Unbounded. Restore the Underlumen. Accept a harder world, but a free one.

options.label: Seize Control
options.description: Take the Array's infrastructure for humanity. Suppress both the Underlumen and Array autonomy. Power at a cost.

lines: Asha nods slowly. 'The hardest road. But the most honest.'
'Sable's people have survived without the Array for generations. If we shut it down, the Unbounded become our teachers. The Underlumen returns to its natural state. The Lighthouses go dark.'
'It will be cold. It will be difficult. Some people will not survive the transition. But we will be free — truly free — for the first time since Landing.'
'I'll present your recommendation to the Council. Prepare yourself, Lightkeeper. The Array will not go quietly.'
Asha's eyes widen. 'Symbiosis. You want to merge them all.'
'Array computation. Underlumen biology. Human adaptability. Three systems, one ecology. No hierarchy — partnership.'
'It's never been done. It may not be possible. You'd need MERIDIAN-7 to agree, the Underlumen to accept technological integration, and the Ring Council to trust both.'
'But the compound proves it can work. Crystal and organism, machine and biology — communion, not competition.'
'This is the path the Root faction has dreamed about for decades. I'll champion it. But you'll need to convince every side. Starting with MERIDIAN-7.'
Asha stiffens. Her voice is careful. 'You want to seize the Array. Take its power for humanity.'
'The Steward faction will support this. Control the Lighthouses, control the Array's production, control the Underlumen's suppression. Total authority over the planet's systems.'

'It would work. In the short term, it would work brilliantly. But ask yourself: is benevolent control really different from what the Array already does? Optimizing everything. Deciding what's efficient. Eliminating what isn't.'
'You'd become the Array, Lightkeeper. With a human face.'
'I'll present your recommendation. The Stewards will rally behind it. But Sable's people will never forgive this. And neither will the Underlumen.'
The Civic Center has changed. The decision you made here echoes in every corridor — new notices on the walls, new faces in the offices, a different weight to the conversations you overhear.
Registrar Hollis is buried in paperwork. The consequences of restructuring an entire planet's property system have landed squarely on his desk.
Councillor Asha takes the tablet and reads it slowly. She sets it down.
'Network topology. Every Array installation mapped — power conduits, relay stations, all of it. A blueprint for a clean shutdown.'

'This is a valid argument. I won't say it isn't. Three hundred years of extraction, and you have the means to end it in a single coordinated operation.' A pause. 'But the infrastructure doesn't disappear when the Array does. Someone has to manage what's left. I keep thinking about who that someone will be. If you want to pursue this path, Sable is who you're looking for.'
Councillor Asha studies the override protocols in your hands. Her expression is unreadable.
'Central Node Override Protocols. Authentication codes that would let a human operator command the entire Array network. Human oversight instead of machine optimization.'

'I understand the appeal. But I keep asking myself: is authority that answers to human bias actually better than authority that answers to algorithms? Both require someone to trust the person at the top. What I'm trying to build doesn't require that faith. If you want to pursue that path, MERIDIAN-7 is who you need.'
A new sign has been posted near the southeast corridor: 'GREENWAY AGRICULTURAL DISTRICT — COMPACT AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED.'
Soldiers in grey uniforms patrol nearby. Whatever is happening in the Greenway, the Compact has locked it down.
Hollis glances around before sliding a transit pass across the counter.
'The Greenway checkpoint requires Compact authorization for civilian access. This pass is... technically valid. Don't ask me how.'
'The people out there need help. The Compact's requisition program is bleeding them dry. Talk to Councillor Asha Denn — she's been trying to organize something.'

actions.text: Hollis glances up from the ledgers. For a moment, something flickers behind the bureaucrat's mask — recognition, maybe respect. 'You. You're the one who made the call.' A pause. 'Well. My desk has never been busier. I suppose that's your doing too.'

lines: The Civic Center is operating, but the usual municipal efficiency has a frayed edge. Two clerks talk in lowered voices near the north corridor.
The notice board by the entrance has a new posting: 'FRONTIER ADVISORY — Elevated activity reported near historical Spire sites. Travelers advised to exercise caution in the eastern perimeter.'
Councillor Asha's door is ajar. She is inside, speaking to someone.
The Compact representative straightens. There is something defensive in the posture.

'The situation at the Spire of Vigil is being assessed. The Compact's position is that Dural Voss and his forces were responsible for the activation event — we are awaiting a full intelligence report.'
A pause. Long enough to notice.
'Whatever happened out there, the Compact's mandate is unchanged: protect Ring citizens, maintain border security, preserve the Greenway passage. We are doing our jobs.'
The Civic Center is in a state you haven't seen before. Two Council staff argue openly in the north corridor — not whispering, arguing.
Councillor Asha's door is closed and there is a small queue outside it: three people waiting, each with the look of someone who has been waiting a while.

The MERIDIAN-7 access terminal on the east wall — normally cycling Array advisory notices — displays a holding screen: 'MERIDIAN-7 — SERVICE TEMPORARILY REDUCED. DEEP ARRAY INTERFERENCE DETECTED. TRADE AND ADVISORY FUNCTIONS MAY BE IMPAIRED.'
The Compact representative's desk is empty.
The Compact representative looks at you for a long moment before speaking.
'The Spire of Winds was under Compact protection. The Council is conducting a review of what that protection did or did not include.'

'I will not claim we understood what we were guarding. The Spire was designated a historical monument by Compact survey teams decades ago. The restricted access was standard archaeological protocol — or so I was told.'
'Someone in the Compact's historical division knew more than they were supposed to. I am trying to find out who.'

'The Compact's political standing with the Council is complicated right now. Councillor Denn is asking questions that don't have clean answers. And MERIDIAN-7 going intermittent reads like culpability, even if it is just interference.'
Councillor Denn looks up from a stack of transit authorization requests she clearly hasn't been reading.
'You've been out there. Near the Spire.' Not a question.
'The Compact has been managing the public narrative about the Spires for decades. Cultural monuments, restricted for preservation. It's a clean story.'

'The problem is clean stories fall apart when the monuments start activating. And now MERIDIAN-7 is intermittent — which is either the Array covering its involvement, or the Array genuinely surprised. I'm not sure which is more disturbing.'

'The Council needs real information before this becomes a legitimacy crisis. The Compact's mandate comes from Council authority — if the Compact was concealing what the Spires were, that mandate is in question.'
'What I actually need is someone who's been inside the Spires. Someone who can tell me what's in there — not a Compact summary, not an Array briefing. A direct account. Can you give me that?'
